name: Deep Bluish Grey-Green
lede: Deep Bluish Grey-Green is a muted, grey-leaning green, Robert Ridgway's darker step down from his own Bluish Grey-Green, with a second life as a Japanese traditional color gloss.

sections.title: One grey-green, two naming systems
sections.body: Ridgway recorded Deep Bluish Grey-Green in 1912, plate XLII, hue 41 triple-prime, tone i, directly below [[bluish-grey-green|Bluish Grey-Green]] on the same card [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary filed this darker name again in 1955, block 150, as a grayish green [2]. The same hue also carries a Japanese traditional gloss in our data, *Sabiasagi* (錆浅葱), "rusted light-blue," an entirely separate naming thread from Ridgway's grammar [3]. Its nearest named neighbors on file are [[serpent]] and [[deep-medici-blue]], at 3.0 to 3.3 CIEDE2000 units [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this grey-green, as photographed, in 332 of 23,781 paintings, 1.4 percent, more common than 65 percent of the named colors we track [5]. It peaks in the 1900s, 20 of 1,674 paintings from that century, 2.0 times the expected rate [5]. Paul Cezanne is its most devoted painter here, in 5 of his 50 works, 5.4 times the baseline rate [5]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, in 37 percent of its 144 strongest matches [5].
